_comment: Frozen SLIM+wire-compat contract constants — the single source of truth both
MUST reproduce byte-for-byte. The copy exists because the thin uv-tool CLI
Both test suites read THIS file and assert their own primitives against it, so
the two copies cannot silently drift apart (a drift -> MLS group-key mismatch ->
connectors silently can't join, or messages get dropped/misrouted). If a change
to the shared wire shape is genuinely intended, update this file deliberately in
the same PR and both suites will re-lock to the new value.

identity._comment: SignerJwt-floor SLIM channel identity constants (#476), keyed byte-for-byte by both copies: backend app.services.slim_identity, CLI mycelium.slim.identity. issuer/audience/alg/curve MUST agree across members or peer verification fails inside the MLS handshake; jwk_kid_is_handle records that a roster JWK's `kid` is the raw @handle. mode_default=psk is the off-by-default posture (#567). The ladder has two rungs, psk and signerjwt.

valid_subkinds._comment: Kind -> allowed subkinds. Backend: app.services.message_format.VALID_SUBKINDS (keyed by the Kind enum). CLI: mycelium.slim.message_format.VALID_SUBKINDS (keyed by the plain string, since the hidden `message send`/`slim send` plumbing takes a raw --kind string). An empty/None subkind is always valid for any kind. The exchange move subkinds counter/accept/reject are the closed negotiation-move vocabulary a coordination reply carries on the wire (counter = any offer incl. the opening one; accept/reject respond to the standing offer); team-formation predates them. ``amend`` revises an earlier message: parents carries the amended message's id, the payload carries the new text, and the read path folds the chain to the newest text.

ping._comment: The payload type a thread's activity surfaces into the room as. The backend PRODUCES it (room_channels.raise_ping, off app.services.message_format.PING_PAYLOAD_TYPE) on every write into a thread; the CLI READS it (mycelium.slim.message_format.ping_of) to draw the one activity line `room watch` shows when a task moves. A ping deliberately carries no prose — only which thread moved, who wrote it and the message id — so payload_fields is the whole of it, and a reader expecting text would draw an empty line instead of the argument the thread exists to absorb. It is also what the backend's participate._addressed_to excludes, so a resident agent consumes a ping silently rather than spending a turn on it: rename the type on one side only and every agent in the room wakes on every thread write. The GUI is the third reader (mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts, ping_of + PING_PAYLOAD_TYPE): it draws the coalesced 'activity in <task>' notice the room sees in place of the thread's prose, so a drift here empties the channel of any sign its threads moved.

notice._comment: The payload type the room's board events surface into its timeline as. Where a ping says a thread moved, a notice says the board did: a task filed, claimed, handed back or resolved. The backend PRODUCES it (room_channels.raise_notice, off app.services.message_format.NOTICE_PAYLOAD_TYPE) at each seam — leases.claim/release/resolve, the memory upsert on a board-row create, and the lease sweep (lease_sweep.py) when a held lease drains past its TTL (`expired`, raised once per lease); the GUI READS it (mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts, notice_of + NOTICE_PAYLOAD_TYPE) to draw the 'New task'/'Claimed'/'Resolved' line the channel shows in sequence with the chat. Like a ping it is excluded from participate._addressed_to, so a resident agent consumes a notice silently rather than waking on it: rename the type on one side and either the timeline goes quiet or every agent wakes on every board write. `data.subkind` is one of `subkinds` (a closed set); `data` always carries `subkind` and `key`, and a `filed` notice also carries the board `kind` so the line reads 'New decision' not always 'New task'. `floor` is the one notice about a thread rather than a task: raised by room_channels.hold_floor/release_floor when whose turn it is changes, with `key` the thread's short id, `by` the holder, `speakers` the comma-joined handles given the floor (absent when the holder alone has it) and `released` set when it opens back up. `upstream` says the external thing a row points at changed (a pull request's review or CI moved, or it merged or closed): raised by the status watcher (app/services/status/watch.py) when a provider's answer for a linked ref differs from the room's last one, with `change` one of `upstream_changes`, `ref` the provider's id for it (`owner/repo#123`), `url`, `label` the provider's own word for its state now, and `at` when the source changed. Nobody writes it and it wakes nobody: the wake digest lists it on the `Board:` line of whoever holds, was given or filed the row (a merge to everyone), and nothing raises a wake for it.

shared_secret._comment: mint_shared_secret is keyed on workspace/room only (agent ignored). HMAC-SHA256(master_secret, 'workspace/room').hexdigest().

urn._comment: Room-scoped episode/topic URN forms. Backend: message_format.episode_urn(room, session) / message_format.topic_urn(room). CLI connector: _room_episode(room) / _room_topic(room) with the 'live' session literal. Frontend: mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts liveEpisodeUrn(room), which is how the channel tells the room's own messages from a thread's.

envelope._comment: A frozen serialized 'exchange' message content dict. The backend produces this via message_format.envelope_to_dict(message_format.build_envelope(kind=exchange, ...)); the CLI produces the same dict via message_format.build_reply_content(...). The two serializers must agree byte-for-byte or a connector's reply fails the backend persister's parse_envelope.

knowledge._comment: A frozen serialized 'knowledge:distillation' message — the memory-sync wire shape. The backend PRODUCES it via memory_sync.build_knowledge_envelope(room, write, recipients) + KnowledgeWrite.to_payload() (serialized with message_format.envelope_to_dict); the CLI PARSES it via slim/message_format.payload_data_of. The two must agree byte-for-byte on the payload.data write fields or cross-machine memory sync silently drifts. build_knowledge_envelope mints a fresh random message.id per call, so 'expected_envelope.header.message.id' is the sentinel 'MESSAGE_ID_PLACEHOLDER' — the backend test normalizes the produced id to it before comparing (the id is not part of the shared contract; every other field is).
